{
  "analyses": [
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-1145-3209978-3210046",
      "title": "Characterizing and Supporting Question Answering in Human-to-Human Communication",
      "research_question": "How do information workers exchange and later retrieve question-answer information in enterprise email, and can corresponding answers in email threads be automatically identified?",
      "methodology": "The authors surveyed 924 employees of a large technology company about question-answer information in work email and analyzed the Avocado corporate email collection, which contains 938,035 emails from 279 employees of a defunct IT company. They extracted candidate question sentences using rule-based patterns, filtered them with crowdsourced judgments, and took the top ten paragraphs from subsequent messages as candidate answers. Three annotators judged question validity, enduring value, and answer relevance, producing an Avocado QA set of 1,695 unique questions, after which several retrieval models were evaluated with ten-fold cross-validation using MAP and average recall.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Question-answer information is a frequent workplace-email retrieval need: 98.7% of surveyed respondents reported needing to locate an answer from their mailbox at least once in the preceding month.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.2 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The constructed QA dataset contains 1,695 unique question sentences, each paired with ten candidate answer paragraphs, with one or more candidates allowed to be relevant.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2 Question/Answer Pairs Annotation; 6.1 Dataset and Evaluation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Selecting the paragraph or paragraphs that answer a question was substantially more subjective than recognizing questionhood: reported inter-annotator agreement was 0.48 for answer selection versus 0.91 for question validity.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2 Question/Answer Pairs Annotation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The operational QA unit is an individual extracted question sentence matched to answer paragraphs independently, rather than a joint representation of all propositions or subquestions in an email.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4 Data Sets and Task Definition; 4.2 Question/Answer Pairs Annotation"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The proposed neural matching model outperformed TF-IDF, BiMPM, and decomposable attention on Avocado QA, reaching MAP 48.95 and average recall 82.34 before external pretraining.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6.3 Results on Avocado QA Dataset"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Pretraining on the out-of-domain SemEval 2017 community-QA data increased MAP from 48.95 to 50.75 and average recall from 82.34 to 82.55.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6.4 Results on Avocado QA Dataset with Pre-training"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The paper does not explicitly annotate whether a reply answers all versus only some of several questions contained in the same email.",
        "Approval, rejection, and other short responses are not modeled as proposition-scoped acts over multiple antecedent propositions.",
        "Question extraction favors sentences beginning with one of six wh-words and ending with a question mark, so many indirect, declarative, elliptical, or differently formatted questions can be omitted.",
        "Emails longer than 100 words were filtered during question extraction, which can systematically exclude complex messages containing multiple propositions or questions.",
        "Candidate answers were restricted to the top ten paragraphs of subsequent emails, so later or differently segmented answers can be missed.",
        "Answer-selection agreement of 0.48 indicates substantial ambiguity in the ground-truth linkage.",
        "The survey came from one technology company and had a 15% response rate.",
        "The derived Avocado QA annotations were not accompanied by a release link in the paper inspected, although the underlying Avocado collection is distributed separately by the Linguistic Data Consortium."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "work_email_answer_retrieval_is_common": 0.99,
        "avocado_qa_has_1695_questions": 0.99,
        "answer_selection_is_subjective": 0.99,
        "qa_unit_is_individual_question_sentence": 0.98,
        "proposed_model_outperforms_baselines": 0.99,
        "external_pretraining_improves_map": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "The survey analysis uses 924 complete responses from employees of a large technology company.",
        "Almost all respondents reported retrieving answers from work email during the preceding month.",
        "The Avocado collection contains 938,035 corporate emails associated with 279 employees.",
        "Questions are extracted and evaluated primarily as individual sentences rather than as complete multi-question messages.",
        "For each extracted question, ten paragraphs from later emails are considered as candidate answers.",
        "The annotation procedure permits multiple answer paragraphs to be relevant to one question.",
        "The resulting Avocado QA dataset contains 1,695 unique questions.",
        "Human agreement is considerably lower for selecting answers than for recognizing valid questions.",
        "The proposed neural model performs better than the reported retrieval and neural baselines.",
        "SemEval pretraining gives a modest additional improvement."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/uploads/prod/2018/04/EmailQA_SIGIR18.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "manual-849c5f1c6d",
      "title": "Automatically Selecting Answer Templates to Respond to Customer Emails",
      "research_question": "Can historical customer-email question-answer associations be learned well enough to select and combine response templates for new emails that may contain multiple questions?",
      "methodology": "The authors identify question and answer sentences using learned key phrases, then map questions to answer sentences using lexical overlap weighted by inverse document frequency and a positional heuristic. They evaluate question-answer mapping on 30 manually annotated query-first-response pairs from the Pine-Info mailing list and response generation on 1,320 real mobile-phone contact-center query-response pairs with 570 response templates. The contact-center experiments use 920 pairs for training and 400 for testing, with and without automatic triage, and evaluate both exact response agreement and partial correctness at the level of answered questions.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The system explicitly decomposes an email containing multiple questions and attempts to associate each individual question with an answer and ultimately a response template.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3 Problem Definition; 5.2 Mapping Questions to Answers"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The Pine-Info sample directly demonstrates incomplete first replies: 30 initiating emails contained 43 annotated questions but only 36 question-answer mappings in the first responses, and the paper's worked example has two questions but only one marked answer.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.1 Contact Center Data; 7.3 Experiments"
        },
        {
          "finding": "In the 30 Pine-Info pairs, an initiating email averaged 1.43 questions, its first response averaged 1.3 answers, and there were 1.2 mapped question-answer pairs per pair of messages.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.1 Contact Center Data"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors operationalize partial reply coverage explicitly: if a two-question message receives a system response matching the human response for only one question, that response receives 50% partial credit.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.2 Measures"
        },
        {
          "finding": "On Pine-Info, the automatic mapping recovered 28 of the 36 manually identified question-answer mappings, reported as 77.78% correct.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.3 Experiments"
        },
        {
          "finding": "On the contact-center test set, exact response reproduction was 61% and partial correctness 73.4% without triage; with triage these rose to 79.1% and 84.8%, respectively.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.3 Experiments"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The contact-center responses used an average of 2.3 templates, which the authors interpret as indicating roughly two key questions per customer query.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.1 Contact Center Data"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Some customer questions cannot be handled with the predefined template inventory because agents sometimes compose a new reply instead.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7.3 Experiments"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Only 30 Pine-Info query-response pairs were manually annotated for question-answer scope.",
        "The Pine-Info evaluation examines only the first response after the initiating email, even though unanswered questions may be addressed later in the thread.",
        "The larger contact-center corpus is from one mobile-phone support process and is not presented as a publicly released dataset.",
        "Question and answer detection is sentence-based and relies on learned key phrases, so implicit questions, multi-sentence propositions, and short context-dependent replies may be missed.",
        "The question-answer mapping relies heavily on lexical overlap and relative position, which can fail when an answer uses different vocabulary or addresses questions out of order.",
        "Partial correctness compares system output with the human response rather than providing a comprehensive descriptive annotation of all human partial-reply behaviors.",
        "The template formulation assumes that relevant replies can usually be represented by a finite template inventory, while the paper acknowledges free-form agent responses outside that inventory.",
        "The study does not explicitly model one response clause as jointly scoped over several distinct antecedent propositions."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "multiple_questions_are_decomposed": 0.99,
        "first_replies_can_leave_questions_unanswered": 0.99,
        "pine_question_answer_averages": 0.99,
        "partial_coverage_is_explicitly_scored": 0.99,
        "pine_mapping_accuracy": 0.99,
        "contact_center_partial_accuracy": 0.99,
        "responses_use_multiple_templates": 0.98,
        "templates_do_not_cover_all_replies": 0.98
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "A customer email can contain several questions that require several response templates.",
        "The method first identifies individual questions and then maps them to corresponding answer material.",
        "The first reply in an email thread does not necessarily answer every question in the initiating message.",
        "The 30 Pine-Info initiating emails contain 43 manually identified questions and 36 mapped question-answer pairs in their first replies.",
        "One illustrated Pine-Info message contains two questions while its first response supplies only one annotated answer.",
        "Partial correctness is measured according to how many question-specific parts of the human response are reproduced.",
        "The mobile-phone contact-center corpus contains 1,320 query-response pairs and 570 templates.",
        "The contact-center responses contain multiple templates on average.",
        "Automatic triage substantially improves exact response matching in the reported experiment.",
        "Human agents sometimes write responses that do not use any predefined template."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/07/Papers/268.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-1016-j-pragma-2010-04-002",
      "title": "A coding scheme for question–response sequences in conversation",
      "research_question": "How can naturally occurring question-response sequences be operationalized with a coding scheme that permits systematic cross-linguistic comparison?",
      "methodology": "The paper documents the coding scheme developed for a ten-language comparative project using naturally occurring ordinary conversation from dyadic and multiparty interactions. Each participating researcher was asked to code at least 350 questions, and the scheme was refined through two cycles of pilot coding and collaborative evaluation across languages. It operationalizes question form and action, multi-question turns, recipient selection, response occurrence and type, timing, modality, and the form and polarity of answers.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The scheme explicitly marks a 'through-produced' multi-question when two or more questions are delivered as one query in a single turn.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2 The coding scheme, item (4)"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors state that through-produced multi-questions require separate treatment because they can mix polar and content questions and the response often answers only one component question.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2 The coding scheme, item (4)"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Question responses are coded separately as no response, a non-answer response, an answer, or indeterminate, allowing unanswered questions to be distinguished from indirect or evasive responses.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2 The coding scheme, item (17)"
        },
        {
          "finding": "For polar questions that receive an answer, the scheme codes whether the answer confirms or disconfirms the questioned proposition rather than equating confirmation mechanically with the words yes or no.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2 The coding scheme, item (23)"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Polar-answer form distinguishes repetitions from interjections and marked interjections, and the repetition category includes partial as well as full repeats of the antecedent question.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2 The coding scheme, item (24)"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Some planned coding of sequential position was excluded from the comparative analysis because the researchers could not obtain adequate validity or reliability for those categories.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "1 Introduction"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The data are ordinary spoken conversation rather than workplace email or enterprise dialogue.",
        "This article primarily specifies the coding methodology; language-specific empirical distributions are reported in other papers in the special issue.",
        "It does not report a quantified prevalence of partial answers to through-produced multi-questions.",
        "The scheme identifies a turn as containing multiple questions but does not provide a full proposition-by-proposition alignment matrix between every response span and every antecedent question component.",
        "It does not directly study enterprise approval or rejection acts, although confirmation and disconfirmation of polar questions provide a related distinction.",
        "Some sequential-position variables were abandoned because adequate validity or reliability could not be achieved."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": false
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "through_produced_multiquestions_are_explicitly_coded": 0.99,
        "responses_often_target_only_one_component": 0.99,
        "none_nonanswer_answer_are_distinguished": 0.99,
        "confirmation_is_proposition_oriented": 0.99,
        "partial_repeats_are_recognized": 0.99,
        "sequential_position_categories_had_reliability_problems": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "The coding scheme was created for comparative analysis across ten languages.",
        "Researchers worked with naturally occurring ordinary conversation rather than elicited questionnaire responses.",
        "Each language researcher was asked to code at least 350 questions.",
        "A turn containing two or more questions delivered as a single query receives a dedicated multi-question code.",
        "Multi-question turns are treated specially partly because a response can answer only one of their questions.",
        "The scheme distinguishes complete absence of a response from a response that fails to answer the question directly.",
        "Indirect responses and expressions such as uncertainty can be coded as non-answers.",
        "An answer to a polar question is analyzed as confirmation or disconfirmation of the proposition.",
        "A confirming or disconfirming response may use a partial repeat rather than a bare yes or no.",
        "The researchers removed some sequential-position coding from comparative analysis because its reliability or validity was inadequate."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.researchgate.net/publication/50435655_A_coding_scheme_for_question-response_sequences_in_conversation",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-5087-dad-2020-104",
      "title": "Modelling Structures for Situated Discourse",
      "research_question": "How should discourse structure be modeled when multiparty linguistic moves interact with nonlinguistic events in a situated environment, including structures that cannot be represented as a simple tree?",
      "methodology": "The authors compare two discourse annotations of STAC, a corpus of multiparty chat from an online Settlers of Catan environment: an initial chat-only annotation and a later situated annotation that also represents game events. Chats are segmented into elementary discourse units and linked with SDRT-style rhetorical relations, while complex discourse units can group several elementary units into a single relational argument. Four initially naive annotators were trained on 22 negotiation dialogues comprising 560 turns, followed by four expert annotators and at least five revision stages that produced consensus gold annotations. The paper quantitatively compares attachments and structures between the linguistic-only and situated versions of the corpus.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Responses can have multiple distinct antecedents: in one analyzed exchange, a single acknowledgement is interpreted as responding jointly to three preceding negative replies.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.3 Three points about multiparty dialogue"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Such multi-antecedent links are not rare in this corpus: 928 of 12,588 discourse units in the chat-only annotations, about 7%, are classified as truly non-treelike because they receive incoming links from different source units.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.3 Three points about multiparty dialogue"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The corpus contains simultaneously developing dialogue threads, and even an individual speaker can participate in several independent threads at once.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.3 Three points about multiparty dialogue"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Offers and their acceptances or refusals are modeled propositionally through Question-Answer Pair relations: a completed trade can function as a yes to an offer, while a trade-panel refusal or rejection functions as a no.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.1.1 Rhetorical relations between EEUs"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Complex discourse units allow several antecedent events or replies to be treated jointly as the argument of a later relation; for example, an action can be annotated as the result of an entire sequence of failed offers and refusals rather than of one immediately preceding unit.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.1.2 Complex structures relevant for the situated annotations"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Adding situated events supplied antecedents for all 1,501 chat-only orphan units and created 3,591 links between linguistic and nonlinguistic material.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.1 Preservation of relations"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Local relation preservation was substantially higher than whole-structure preservation: persisting chat-only relations made up 72% of situated chat-to-chat relations, while only 496 of 1,137 chat-only dialogue structures, a little over 43%, were preserved as elementary substructures.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.1 Preservation of relations; 4.2 Preservation of structures"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Pilot annotation agreement was kappa 0.72 for attachment alone and 0.58 when exact attachment and relation label both had to match.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.2 Corpus annotation"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The interaction domain is a strategy game rather than workplace email or enterprise collaboration.",
        "The paper is primarily about discourse structure and situated context, not specifically about unanswered subquestions in compound interrogatives.",
        "Its strongest evidence for joint antecedents concerns multiparty chat and game actions, so transfer to asynchronous email requires empirical validation.",
        "The interpretation of complex and non-treelike attachments depends on SDRT annotation decisions and expert consensus.",
        "Initial attachment-plus-label agreement was only moderate at kappa 0.58 before expert revision.",
        "The represented nonlinguistic context is derived from the game environment and does not encompass every kind of real-world contextual state relevant to workplace communication."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "one_move_can_target_multiple_antecedents": 0.99,
        "non_treelike_units_are_empirically_common": 0.99,
        "overlapping_threads_occur": 0.99,
        "accept_refuse_can_scope_to_offers": 0.98,
        "complex_units_support_joint_antecedent_scope": 0.99,
        "situated_context_resolves_orphans": 0.99,
        "whole_structure_preservation_is_lower": 0.99,
        "annotation_agreement_reported": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "STAC contains multiparty chat situated in an online Settlers of Catan environment.",
        "Discourse units are connected by directed rhetorical relations rather than being constrained to a tree.",
        "A truly non-treelike unit can be linked to two or more different antecedent discourse units.",
        "The chat-only data contain 928 truly non-treelike units among 12,588 discourse units.",
        "One acknowledgement in the corpus is analyzed as jointly addressing three preceding negative responses.",
        "Independent conversational threads can proceed simultaneously.",
        "Offers are represented as structures that can receive acceptance or refusal responses.",
        "A rejection in the game interface can serve the discourse function of a negative answer to an offer.",
        "Several events can be grouped into one complex discourse unit and jointly serve as an antecedent.",
        "Adding game events changes a substantial fraction of discourse attachments inferred from language alone.",
        "The STAC annotations and their annotation manual are linked from the paper."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://aclanthology.org/2020.dnd-11.6.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-1515-text-2003-021",
      "title": "Multi-unit questions in institutional interactions: Sequential organizations and communicative functions",
      "research_question": "What recurrent internal organizations, sequential conditions, and communicative functions characterize multi-unit questioning turns in institutional interaction?",
      "methodology": "The authors compare naturally occurring Swedish institutional interactions from two studies: nine encounters totaling almost six hours across maternal-health booking, social-welfare, criminal-court, and police-interrogation settings, plus 20 doctor consultations totaling about 12.5 hours. They analyze 374 multi-unit questioning turns in terms of their syntactic organization and the semantic, pragmatic, and sequential relationships among component turn-construction units. The analysis combines quantitative distributions with detailed conversation-analytic examination of how questions develop in interaction and how recipients respond or fail to respond.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The combined corpora contain 374 multi-unit questioning turns, representing about 16% of all questioning turns, and about 90% of questioning turns are produced by the institutional professional.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3 Data and their contexts"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Multi-unit questions frequently narrow an initially broader inquiry through particularizing follow-up components; in Hofvendahl's coded component questions, 81% (101 of 124) had a particularizing relation to the preceding head question, compared with 11% generalizing and 7% metacommunicative.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Notes to the analysis of question-component relations"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The paper identifies collateral questions as distinct questions delivered together without a particularizing, generalizing, or paraphrasing relation, usually linked by an explicit or implicit common super-topic.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.3 Some related kinds of question sequences: Paraphrases and collateral questions"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Component questions can remain unanswered during construction of a multi-unit turn: in one analyzed case the initial broad question receives no response and is subsequently replaced or pursued with more specific component questions.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4 MUQTs: Two introductory examples"
        },
        {
          "finding": "A negative response to one component can occasion production of another collateral component, showing that the evolving scope and content of the question package can depend on the recipient's partial response.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.3 Some related kinds of question sequences: Paraphrases and collateral questions"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Generalizing appended questions widen the space of acceptable answers and can relax constraints introduced by preceding alternatives or more specific components.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.4 Generalizing appended questions"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors interpret both narrowing and broadening question components as response-securing strategies: particularization seeks a sufficiently precise answer, whereas generalization makes a wider range of responses acceptable.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6 The communicative functions of MUQTs"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Multi-unit questions are partly interactional accomplishments because an addressee's response or lack of response can influence their progressive production.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "7 Conclusions and suggestions for further research"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The study concerns spoken institutional interaction rather than email or enterprise messaging.",
        "All analyzed activity types are locally dyadic, limiting evidence about multiparty antecedent structure.",
        "The data comprise 29 institutional encounters in Swedish and are concentrated in medical, legal, social-welfare, and related professional settings.",
        "The paper primarily analyzes question design and sequential emergence rather than exhaustively annotating which exact response spans answer which proposition in every multi-unit turn.",
        "Boundaries among categories such as paraphrasing and particularizing are acknowledged to be non-clear-cut.",
        "The paper does not provide a general quantitative rate for how often individual subquestions are left unanswered or jointly answered.",
        "No public corpus release or reproducible annotation package is provided in the article inspected."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "muqts_are_common_in_institutional_questioning": 0.99,
        "particularization_dominates_component_relations": 0.99,
        "collateral_questions_form_question_packages": 0.98,
        "component_questions_can_be_unanswered": 0.99,
        "partial_responses_can_shape_followup_components": 0.98,
        "generalizers_widen_reply_scope": 0.99,
        "question_design_seeks_to_secure_responses": 0.98,
        "muqts_emerge_interactionally": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "The two corpora together contain 374 multi-unit questioning turns.",
        "Multi-unit questioning turns account for about 16% of questioning turns in both corpora.",
        "Institutional professionals produce roughly 90% of the questioning turns.",
        "Question components can narrow, broaden, paraphrase, or stand collaterally to other components.",
        "Particularizing relations are the dominant component relation in Hofvendahl's corpus.",
        "Collateral questions can package several distinct inquiries under a common topic.",
        "An initial question may receive no response before the professional adds more specific questions.",
        "A recipient's negative response to one component can trigger another question component.",
        "Generalizing final components widen the set of responses that can satisfy the questioning turn.",
        "Particularizing and generalizing components serve different ways of securing a response.",
        "The recipient's response behavior can influence how a multi-unit question is progressively constructed."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.researchgate.net/publication/250974735_Multi-unit_questions_in_institutional_interactions_Sequential_organizations_and_communicative_functions",
      "access": "full_text"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
